directAnswer: You can check your graphics card by accessing the Device Manager in Windows or using the System Information tool on macOS.
summary: This guide provides steps to identify your graphics card on both Windows and macOS systems.

sections.heading: Using Device Manager on Windows
sections.body: Device Manager allows you to view all hardware components, including your graphics card.

sections.heading: Using System Information on macOS
sections.body: The System Information tool provides detailed information about your Mac's hardware, including the graphics card.

steps.title: Check Graphics Card on Windows
steps.detail: Right-click on the Start menu, select 'Device Manager', expand the 'Display adapters' section to see your graphics card.

steps.title: Check Graphics Card on macOS
steps.detail: Click the Apple menu, select 'About This Mac', then click 'System Report' and look under 'Graphics/Displays'.

faqs.question: What if my graphics card is not listed?
faqs.answer: If your graphics card is not visible, it may indicate a driver issue or that the card is not properly installed.

faqs.question: Can I check my graphics card using third-party software?
faqs.answer: Yes, software like GPU-Z or HWMonitor can provide detailed information about your graphics card.

faqs.question: How do I update my graphics card drivers?
faqs.answer: You can update drivers through Device Manager on Windows or by visiting the manufacturer's website for macOS.

caveats: Steps may vary slightly depending on your operating system version.
